title: Minimax Neyman Regret of Adaptive Designs under Arbitrary Temporal Drift

proof_attempt_summary: Two D0 solve windows produced a complete logarithmic regret derivation for the original bounded, arbitrarily drifting, chosen-arm feedback model. An independent maximality audit promoted a symmetric-Beta converse to the coefficient-4 lower envelope and the prior-specific pairing gap; correctness reviewers and a fresh main validity consult found no load-bearing defect. The subfield ceiling 6.7 falls below the field floor 7.4; exact full-class coefficient limits, full-class pairing comparison, and practical finite-sample gains remain open, and no Lean formalization was launched.
tldr: For the prescribed centered causal score, bounded fixed tables with arbitrary temporal drift have minimax design regret \(R_T=\Theta(\log(T+1))\). A legal paired finite-arithmetic Newton policy attains the uniform upper bound. Exact Bayes calculations in the original logged-feedback experiment give \(R_T\ge B_{T,\lambda}\) for every integer \(\lambda\ge1\), retaining the uniform-prior bound \((8/3)H(T+1)\). Taking \(\lambda=\lceil\log(T+1)\rceil\) certifies a lower leading coefficient of \(4\), against an upper coefficient of \(60000\). The symmetric identical-arm family incurs at most \(2/\lambda\) extra Bayes regret from paired updates, so it cannot determine the full-class pairing penalty. The worst-case excess causal MSE is exactly \(R_T/T^2\); the exact coefficient and its limit remain open.
gap: The deterministic AIPW theorem of Chen et al. permits aggregate fourth-moment control and positive residual RMS; its lower construction contains a first outcome of order \(T^{1/4}\). The centered logarithmic guarantee of Neopane et al. fixes conditional moments. These results leave the uniformly bounded, arbitrarily drifting joint-centering decision problem unresolved.
fill: The conditional synthetic-loss identity, uniform curvature calculation, explicit Newton certificate, and bounded table converse determine the growth of \(R_T\). The exact MSE translation keeps causal precision as the decision criterion.
